concept.title: Where BPM validation ends and Firefox runtime begins
concept.shortdesc: BPM validates and exports a Firefox Enterprise policy document; Firefox applies the document at runtime outside BPM.

section.title: BPM profile model
section.p: A BPM profile is a saved editing model. It can contain policy values, managed preferences, source information, validation state, preset or CIS-derived values, and raw imported data before export.

section.title: Firefox boundary document
section.p: The exported boundary is a policies.json document with a top-level policies object. BPM validation checks shape, supported policy IDs, channel availability, and known value constraints, but it does not prove how a deployed Firefox installation will behave in every environment.

section.title: Firefox runtime responsibility
section.p: Firefox owns policy loading, operating-system deployment paths, extension installation, certificate trust behavior, network access, and user-visible browser effects. BPM documentation describes the configuration path and known schema facts, not administrator rollout procedures.

section.title: Managed preferences
section.p: Managed preferences are configured through the Firefox Preferences policy. BPM can expose known preferences and preserve advanced values, but preference effects still depend on Firefox runtime support and the selected schema channel.
